title: US equity markets closed — Good Friday (falls BEFORE quarter-end in 2027)
source: NEWS: nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 109,180 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell out of its holiday table by this session. Against the year headers, the 'Good Friday' row parses exactly as ['Friday, April 3', 'Friday, March 26', 'Friday, April 14'] for 2026 / 2027 / 2028 — i.e. the NYSE is closed Friday 2027-03-26. Independently reproduced by computing Easter with the anonymous Gregorian algorithm (Easter 2027 = 2027-03-28, so Good Friday = 2027-03-26; the same computation returns 2026-04-03 for 2026, matching the page). Filed estimate on two counts: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for a securities exchange's own holiday calendar (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:), and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence
notes: DISCOVERED during the opex-2027-03-19 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and it is the first market-CLOSURE entry on this calendar. Why a day the market is shut earns a row: Easter 2027 is unusually early, so Good Friday lands in MARCH, between the 2027-03-19 quarterly triple witching and quarter-end — the configuration that changes the shape of both. The post-witching window normally runs 5 sessions to the following Friday; here it runs 4 (Mon 03-22 through Thu 03-25), and the quarter's final week is a 3-session stub (Mon 03-29, Tue 03-30, Wed 03-31). So the documented post-witching 'unpin' and the quarter-end rebalancing flows are compressed into fewer sessions than the same corridor carries in a normal quarter. In 2026 by contrast Good Friday was 04-03, safely inside Q2 and after quarter-end, which is the usual arrangement. Impact LOW and structural only: a closed session moves nothing by itself and no house playbook is calendar-keyed — it changes how many sessions the flows around it have to clear in, never direction. CORRECTION (initial research, 2026-09-05 — docs/research/events/good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26.md legs 2-4): counting sessions mechanically REFUTES most of the compression claim above. Sessions from the 03-19 witching to the last business day of March are 7 in 2027 — identical to 2026's 7 and MORE than 2025's 6 — so the corridor is mid-range, not compressed; and the '3-session stub week' is a consequence of March 31 falling on a Wednesday, not of the closure (2025's Q1 final week was 1 session, 2026's was 2, so 2027's 3 is the longest of the three). Only ONE compression leg survives: the post-witching week is 4 sessions (Mon 03-22 through Thu 03-25) instead of 5. The rule-keyed quarter-end flows do not move at all — the SEC 497's secondary-reweight test is the second-to-last business day of March (Tue 2027-03-30), effective after the last (Wed 2027-03-31), and deleting 03-26 changes neither. What the seeding note did NOT know is the finding that actually justifies this row: SIFMA's published 2027 US schedule makes 2027-03-26 a FULL fixed-income close plus a 2:00 p.m. ET early close on Thursday 2027-03-25 (the inverse of 2026, where Good Friday itself is a 12:00 p.m. bond half-session), proposed as sifma-bond-early-close-2027-03-25.json in the same PR. HONEST LIMIT ON THE KIND FIELD: EventKind (src/domain/market-events-types.ts) has no slot for an exchange-schedule event, so this is filed 'sector' — the same kind the S&P rebalance market-structure entries use — which is the least-wrong option rather than a right one. Worth a follow-up on whether the union needs a 'market-structure' member; not this lane's call to make.
